_comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH ONLY - the Claude Code CLI does NOT read a project-level .claude/hooks/hooks.json. That filename is a hook source for *plugins*. For a project, the CLI reads hooks from .claude/settings.json (tracked), .claude/settings.local.json (gitignored), ~/.claude/settings.json, managed policy settings, plugin hooks/hooks.json, and skill/agent frontmatter. Keep this file as the annotated original, then merge its .hooks key into .claude/settings.json with tools/sync-hooks-to-settings.sh. If you copy hooks.json into your repo and stop there, your hooks will never fire.
_comment_paths: Commands resolve through ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.} so they fire correctly no matter which directory the tool call ran from. Bare relative paths break as soon as Claude Code works in a subdirectory. Replace the script paths below with your own.
_comment_handler_types: "command" is not the only handler type. Also available: "http" (POST the hook payload to a URL), "mcp_tool" (call a tool on a configured MCP server), "prompt" (LLM yes/no check), and "agent" (agentic verifier). "prompt" and "agent" are tool events only - PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest.
_comment_per_hook_options: Each handler accepts: "timeout" (seconds), "statusMessage" (spinner text), "async" (run in background, do not block the turn), "once" (run a single time then drop), and "if" (permission-rule syntax such as "Bash(git commit *)" that skips the hook unless the tool call matches). Use "if" to avoid spawning a subprocess on every call - but do not narrow a *blocking* gate with it, because a pattern that fails to match is a silent hole rather than a loud failure.
